targets.title: Student understanding of graph slope and area under a graph: A comparison of physics and nonphysics students
targets.evidence_quote: In this paper, we present a replication study of the original work of Susac et al. [7] in which we compare the performance of physics and economics students using the identical questions from the original work about graph slope and area under the graph in the context of physics and finance.
targets.outcome_quote: The findings broadly confirm the results of Susac et al.; that is, physics students perform better than nonphysics students. While economics students likely have better prior knowledge on finance context than psychology students, the physics students still outperform them on the finance questions. In contrast to the work by Susac et al., both groups of students had the same visit duration on the graphs, consequently proving total dwell time to be an inadequate predictor of performance.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Physics performance advantage agrees, but authors explicitly contrast the dwell-time result. Broad confirmation is attached to the performance comparison, not an overall verdict superseding the explicit contrast. Additional question-type contrasts in discussion reinforce mixed.
